caption:
Sam Bankman-Fried's FTX and Alameda put $500 million into Anthropic before FTX collapsed.
The bankruptcy estate sold those shares in 2024 for about $1.34 billion.
At Anthropic's proposed IPO price of $70 to $78, the same shares would be worth about $31 to $35 billion.

Should the estate have waited, or was selling the right call?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

paragraphs.text: The Anthropic shares that Sam Bankman-Fried's FTX and Alameda Research bought for $500 million would be worth roughly $31 billion to $35 billion at the price range Anthropic set for its initial public offering, according to calculations published by crypto.news on November 11, 2026. The FTX bankruptcy estate sold the same shares in 2024 for about $1.34 billion.
How the stake was built and sold

The investment came through Alameda Research Ventures, the venture arm of Bankman-Fried's trading firm, and gave the two companies an initial stake of about 13.56 percent in Anthropic, according to crypto.news and Cryptopolitan. Later funding rounds diluted that stake to about 7.84 percent by early 2024.

FTX collapsed into bankruptcy in late 2022, and the estate set out to sell its holdings to repay customers and creditors. In March 2024, CNBC reported that the estate had agreed to sell nearly two thirds of its Anthropic shares for $884 million, with the largest piece, close to $500 million, going to ATIC Third International Investment, a firm aligned with Abu Dhabi's Mubadala. Jane Street, where Bankman-Fried once worked, agreed to buy almost $100 million of the shares.

Judge John Dorsey approved the sale, and the first batch of about 29.47 million shares closed in April 2024 for $884.1 million, crypto.news reported. A second batch of about 15 million shares followed in June 2024 for $452 million. Both batches sold at close to $30 per share, for a combined total of about $1.34 billion. Other buyers included funds managed by Fidelity, HOF Capital and G Squared.

Anthropic filed updated IPO documents on November 10, 2026, setting a range of $70 to $78 per share for a listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, according to crypto.news. The company completed a 10 for 1 stock split on September 17, 2026, which turned the roughly 44.54 million shares FTX sold into about 445.4 million shares.

At $70 per share, that block would be worth about $31.18 billion. At $78, it would be worth about $34.74 billion, nearly 26 times what the estate received in 2024. The block bought by the Mubadala-linked buyer alone would be worth roughly $11.7 billion to $13 billion at the proposed range, crypto.news calculated. The publication noted that the estate no longer owns the shares and that the IPO price has not been finalized.

Other estimates are higher. Trending Topics, assuming valuations between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion, put the value of the former FTX stake at about $41 billion to $54 billion. Cryptopolitan estimated about $37 billion at a possible opening price near $83 per share.

The timing was not arbitrary. When the shares were sold, an IPO was not in sight and Anthropic had been valued at about $18 billion, according to Trending Topics and CNBC. The estate needed cash to pay customers, who were set to receive 118 percent of their claims. Some customers have argued that the shares may have been bought with customer funds.

Bankman-Fried was sentenced in March 2024 to 25 years in prison after a jury convicted him on seven counts of fraud and conspiracy, and the court ordered him to forfeit $11 billion, Cryptopolitan noted. The Anthropic stake was not the only early bet the estate sold before a big rise: Alameda's stake in Robinhood was bought back by Robinhood for $606 million in 2023, and a $200,000 bet on Anysphere, the maker of Cursor, was liquidated at cost.

The gap between $1.34 billion and a possible $35 billion shows how fast private AI valuations have moved since 2024. It is also a reminder that the estate's goal was to repay customers with certainty at the time, not to hold a bet on a company whose public listing was still years away.
The final IPO price and Anthropic's first trading days will settle how large the missed gain really is, for the estate and for the buyers who took the shares at about $30 each.
